sources.t: Mobile connectivity you can count on
sources.f: Published 3 June 2026; Ofcom opened a discussion on reliable mobile connectivity and the changes needed across industry, government and other stakeholders.
sources.g: A discussion paper and national improvement agenda do not prove current service at an exact premises.

sources.t: Signal struggles on trains widespread
sources.f: Published 3 June 2026; Ofcom reported poor mobile performance across measured railway segments and called for coordinated improvement.
sources.g: Rail measurement results are transport-corridor evidence, not fixed-broadband parcel truth.

sources.t: Affordability of communications services
sources.f: Updated 4 February 2026; Ofcom summarises affordability research and monitoring of broadband social-tariff availability, awareness and take-up.
sources.g: Affordability and take-up evidence does not establish provider coverage at an address.

sources.t: Money saving tips for phone, broadband and pay-TV
sources.f: Published 1 July 2026; consumer guidance covers contracts, switching, social tariffs and ways to reduce communications bills.
sources.g: Consumer savings guidance does not prove service orderability for a parcel.

sources.t: New Ofcom research reveals how to cut phone and internet bills
sources.f: Published 26 February 2026 and updated 30 June 2026; Ofcom reported pricing, bundling and social-tariff findings.
sources.g: Market pricing and consumer-engagement data are not exact-address connectivity evidence.

sources.t: Social tariffs: Cheaper broadband and phone packages
sources.f: Updated 22 June 2026; the official page lists eligibility, prices and provider social-tariff offers.
sources.g: Provider tariff listings explicitly require separate coverage checks and cannot be promoted to parcel truth.

sources.t: Use an Ofcom-accredited price comparison site
sources.f: Updated 17 July 2026; Ofcom lists accredited comparison services audited for accessibility, accuracy and transparency.
sources.g: Product comparison accreditation does not confirm network availability at a premises.

sources.t: Switching off the UK's 2G and 3G mobile networks: customer advice
sources.f: Updated 29 May 2026; Ofcom explains completed 3G closures, planned 2G closures and customer-device implications.
sources.g: National technology-transition guidance is not exact parcel connectivity evidence.

sources.t: 3G and 2G switch-off: expectations of mobile providers
sources.f: Updated 29 May 2026; Ofcom sets regulatory expectations for provider conduct during 2G and 3G network closures.
sources.g: Provider obligations and national timelines do not establish local service quality or availability.

sources.t: 2G and 3G switch-off advice for IoT and third-party device suppliers
sources.f: Updated 19 June 2026; Ofcom advises device suppliers on customer support during the transition from legacy mobile networks.
sources.g: Device-transition guidance is not evidence of fixed or mobile service at an exact address.

sources.t: Telecommunications Market Data Update
sources.f: Updated 23 July 2026; Ofcom reports Q1 2026 fixed-line, broadband, mobile subscription, revenue and usage trends.
sources.g: National quarterly market totals are highly aggregated and cannot prove parcel orderability.

sources.t: March 2026 Project Gigabit contract progress
sources.f: Updated 20 July 2026; monthly contract-level management information uses rounded figures and notes data-ingestion lag.
sources.g: Rounded, lagged contract snapshots are not current exact-premises evidence.

sources.t: April 2026 Project Gigabit contract progress
sources.f: Updated 20 July 2026; BDUK publishes an April snapshot of initial-scope contracted and built premises.
sources.g: Initial-scope management data requires current UPRN and provider validation.

sources.t: May 2026 Project Gigabit contract progress
sources.f: Updated 20 July 2026; the release warns that supplier resubmissions reduced some previously reported built-premises counts.
sources.g: Administrative revisions demonstrate why monthly aggregates cannot be treated as parcel truth.

sources.t: June 2026 Project Gigabit contract progress
sources.f: Updated 20 July 2026; BDUK reports contract-level figures as of 17 June with rounding and ingestion-lag cautions.
sources.g: Monthly programme management information is not a live retail service check.

sources.t: July 2026 Project Gigabit contract progress
sources.f: Updated 20 July 2026; the July snapshot reports initial-scope contracted and built premises using data held on 16 July.
sources.g: A recent aggregate snapshot still does not confirm an individual premises can order service.

sources.t: Project Gigabit network build contract Cumbria
sources.f: Official guidance records the Fibrus Cumbria contract and planned delivery to hard-to-reach premises.
sources.g: Contract plans and maps are subject to change and do not prove current service at a parcel.

sources.t: Project Gigabit network build contract North Northumberland
sources.f: Official guidance records the Borderlink contract, anticipated build and the need for detailed planning before connections become available.
sources.g: Awarded scope and anticipated availability are not a current provider order check.

sources.t: Project Gigabit network build contract North Dorset
sources.f: Official guidance records the Wessex Internet contract and notes that target premises may change during detailed planning.
sources.g: Historic contract scope cannot establish present exact-address service.

sources.t: Project Gigabit network build contract Teesdale
sources.f: Official guidance records the Borderlink Teesdale contract and planned network construction for hard-to-reach premises.
sources.g: A contract award and planned build are not evidence of current retail orderability.
